title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-breadcrumbs
content:
Summary / intent:
- Quick scratchpad for the throughput regression noticed Nov 2 -> Nov 3 on the prod serving cluster for model rwd-7b-v2. Collecting commands run, raw outputs/snippets, hypotheses, and next steps. Use this to hand off to SRE/Runtime team or to attach to INF-4821.

Observed symptoms:
- Overall p50 token latency increased from ~42ms to ~85ms for rwd-7b-v2 on hosted-api route /v1/generate between 2024-11-02 01:00 UTC and 2024-11-03 06:00 UTC.
- Throughput (tokens/s per GPU) dropped ~35% during peak workload.
- GPU utilization (nvidia-smi) dropped from ~74% to ~40% at same request rate.
- Average batch size reported in runtime logs fell from ~12 to ~3.
- KV-cache hit rate (percent) remained stable (~18%) -> suggests not cache regression.

Why I think continuous-batching is implicated:
- Runtime logs show a spike in repeated small batch flush events at the same time latency regressed.
- Config rollout: there was a change to batching policy config rolled out to Dedicated/Hosted yesterday (auto-batching timeout bumped from 6ms -> 40ms for debugging) per PR #238 (sandbox); TL;DR possible mis-translation of ms->s at config layer.
- Small batches -> lower GPU efficiency, explains throughput drop and GPU util decline.

Commands run (local reproductions / instruments):
1) Query serving metrics API for batch size distribution (time window 2024-11-02T00:00 -> 2024-11-04T00:00):
$ curl -s "https://metrics.internal.redwood/api/v1/query_range?query=batch_size_distribution{model=\"rwd-7b-v2\"}&start=2024-11-02T00:00:00Z&end=2024-11-04T00:00:00Z&step=60s" | jq .
- snippet: "buckets: [1: 2100, 2: 4500, 4: 7200, 8: 1200, 16: 50]" -> heavy weight at 1-4.

2) Grep runtime logs for batching timeouts / flush triggers:
$ kubectl -n serving logs serving-runtime-abcde --since=48h | grep -i "batch_timeout" -n | tail -n 50
- found repeating lines like: "[2024-11-03T05:13:21.334Z] INFO BatchFlush reason=batch_timeout configured=40ms actual_wait=40ms size=2" (many occurrences)

3) Inspect active config on control-plane for hosted-api routes:
$ curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" https://controlplane.internal.redwood/api/v1/routes/rwd-7b-v2/batching-config | jq .
- returns (text): "{ \"enabled\": true, \"max_batch_size\": 64, \"batch_timeout_ms\": 40, \"adaptive\": true }"
- note: batch_timeout_ms=40 (intended to be 4 ms) - suspicious.

4) Check kernel-level scheduling / socket backlog to rule out networking backlog:
$ sudo ss -s on GPU node during replay -> no abnormal TCP drops, accept queue ok.

5) Replayed load in staging to reproduce (k6 + scripted client):
- baseline: client pps=200, concurrency=180, prompt len ~60 tokens.
- staging with batch_timeout_ms=40 -> batch sizes collapse to 2-4; p50 token latency doubled; GPU util ~38%.
- staging with batch_timeout_ms=6 -> batch sizes revert to 10-14; p50 ~45ms; GPU util ~72%.

Error/snippet logs collected:
- runtime: "WARN: TSVBench: batch_flush triggered by timeout, size=2, last_enqueue_age=41ms"
- runtime: "DEBUG batching: requested max_wait_ms=40 but internal timer granularity ~10ms -> jitter"
- envoy: "upstream_reset: connection termination by peer" (spikes aligned with small-batch periods)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Misconfiguration: batch_timeout was set to 40 instead of intended 4 or 6 ms due to unit mismatch in control-plane YAML/UI -> leading to more frequent flushes and smaller batches. (High confidence based on config + repro)
2) Adaptive batching logic regression: the adaptive algorithm now biases towards lower latency at cost of throughput when it sees increased inter-arrival variance; a recent change to adaptive heuristics might have changed thresholds. (Medium confidence)
3) Downstream client behavior changed (more bursty short requests), causing small batches; less likely because other models/routes didn't show the same drop. (Low confidence)
4) Kernel timer granularity/jitter combined with higher timeout interacts poorly (edge case) producing more frequent timeouts. (Low/Medium)

Root-cause candidate: config rollout error (units) + interaction with timer granularity.

Immediate mitigation steps taken:
- Rolled back control-plane batching-config for rwd-7b-v2 to batch_timeout_ms=6 at 2024-11-03T07:12 UTC (manual rollback via CP API).
- Verified staging replay: performance restored.
- Notified infra-deploys + SRE to hold any batching-config automated rollouts.
- Opened INF-4821 and linked PR #238 for investigation.

Notes for follow-up / long-term fixes:
- Add stricter schema validation in control-plane for batching_config units (enforce ms int range 1..1000 and add UI hint).
- Add an automatic regression test: replay with synthetic traffic and assert batch_size_distribution mean >= 8 for model rwd-7b-v2 at given concurrency.
- Add alert: if average batch size drops >33% vs baseline for 15m, fire a paging policy.
- Investigate timer granularity effects on host kernels used in serving fleet; maybe tune the internal timer or use high-res timers.
- Expand telemetry: include explicit per-batch flush reason tag (size_limit | timeout | backpressure) in metrics to simplify triage.

Next immediate steps I will do (items I may not have time for):
- Attach full kubectl logs extract to INF-4821 (need to upload to JIRA).
- Pair with Priya tomorrow 10:30 UTC to review adaptive batching PR history and diff for the last month.
- Draft a one-pager for PMs explaining tradeoffs between batch_timeout tuning and latency/throughput.

Notes / timestamps of key ops:
- 2024-11-03 05:40 UTC: First alert from automated perf guard (p50 token latency).
- 2024-11-03 06:10 UTC: Initial grep of logs, observed batch_timeout lines.
- 2024-11-03 06:45 UTC: Confirmed control-plane config shows 40ms.
- 2024-11-03 07:12 UTC: Manual rollback to 6ms.
- 2024-11-03 07:26 UTC: Metrics show p50 trending back down, avg batch size increasing.

Quick reference of useful commands (for whoever picks this up):
- Get control-plane config: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" https://controlplane.internal.redwood/api/v1/routes/<route>/batching-config | jq .
- Fetch runtime logs: kubectl -n serving logs <pod> --since=72h | egrep "batch_flush|batch_timeout|flush reason"
- Batch size distribution query (prometheus-ish): curl -s "https://metrics.internal.redwood/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))"

If you take this on: please keep this doc updated with timeline + rollouts and paste any PR diffs that touch batching heuristics.

-- Jamie
